entries.title: Ezekiel 8:1
segments: In the sixth year; of Jehoiachin's captivity,

. 
 
vv 1-14. 
 
God's holy eyes continually behold all the abominations which are practised by the wicked in secret places; and so far as he chooses, he reveals them to the view of others.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:2
segments: A likeness; "a likeness as the appearance of a man,"

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:3
segments:
In the visions of God; he was carried to Jerusalem only in a vision, not bodily; but the idolatrous rites there represented to him actually existed. 
 
  The inner gate; next to the temple lay the inner court, or court of the priests; then the outer, or court of the Israelites.  The gate here named seems to have led from the inner to the outer court on the north side; but the exact determination of the various localities named in this chapter is difficult.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:11
segments: Ancients; elders, who ought to have been foremost in maintaining the purity of God's worship.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:14
segments: Women weeping for Tammuz; Tammuz answers to the Adonis of the Greeks, a deified mortal, whose death the women annually lamented with idolatrous rites.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:16
segments:
The inner court; that of the priests, whence it appears that these men were priests. 
 
  Their backs toward the temple--worshipped the sun; the priests were appointed by God to minister at his altar, and intercede with him for the people.
That these should worship the sun, with their backs towards God's temple, was the crowning act of wickedness.

entries.title: Ezekiel 8:17
segments:
Put the branch to their nose; after the manner of the ancient Parsees, who worshipped the rising sun holding in their left hand a bundle of twigs. 
 
vv 17-18. 
 
When they who are set for the defence of true religion become leaders of the people in superstition and wickedness, the community becomes speedily corrupted in every part, and ripe for God's desolating judgments.
